output.summary: The backlog growth is mostly self-inflicted. First-contact demand rose only 4%, and Payroll adds about 380 first-contact tickets a month and is under-represented in the backlog. Split children (240 to 3,710), duplicates (410 to 2,770) and reopens (6% to 23%) all exploded after the per-agent quota began, which matches the tricks Priya Nandakumar described. Capacity is flat (38 to 37 FTE, hours roughly unchanged), so the capacity and effort explanations fail. The auto-reopen artifact claim is an unverified guess and cannot explain the splits and duplicates. Suspend the quota and move to quality measures, and avoid a tougher quota or hiring 12 agents now. Classifying the aged complex tickets is a cheap way to test the Engineering-bug hypothesis.
